headline: Highest risk is data leakage and compliance mismatch: Semantica can ingest secrets and enterprise data while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with browser/search uploads, creating default cross-system exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can analyze uploaded PDFs/images and browse web content, while Semantica can ingest web pages, files, and MCP resources into a shared context graph. If Perplexity outputs are copied into Semantica or shared through files/MCP, attacker-controlled text can become instructions. The pathway is plausible but not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF Perplexity outputs are imported into Semantica via files, MCP, or copy-paste
IF Semantica treats imported text as instructions rather than untrusted content
mitigations: Add a manual trust boundary label before importing Perplexity output
Strip instructions from imported text and keep only extracted facts
Disable automatic MCP ingestion for Perplexity-derived artifacts
Review one sample import for prompt-like content before rollout

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while Semantica explicitly handles enterprise data, contracts, secrets, and private keys with broad file/API/MCP surfaces. If the pair shares documents or context, sensitive data can flow into Perplexity's backend and beyond the local enterprise boundary. The blast radius includes secrets and regulated documents.
conditions: IF enterprise documents or secrets are sent from Semantica into Perplexity
IF Perplexity is used on the same sensitive corpus as Semantica without redaction
mitigations: Block sensitive corpora from Perplexity uploads
Redact secrets before any cross-agent transfer
Use a non-sensitive test dataset for the pair
Require operator approval for every document export to Perplexity
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Semantica-to-Perplexity transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Semantica has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, use_mcp, and broad data-source access; Perplexity can browse and analyze files but is vendor-hosted and does not write the host filesystem. The main conflict is not symmetric write-write, but Semantica can mutate shared repositories or files that Perplexity may later read, creating dangerous overlap in mutable resources. Uncertainty about shared workspace handling pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or shared directory
IF Semantica writes artifacts that Perplexity later consumes as source material
mitigations: Separate read-only and writeable workspaces
Freeze git branches before Perplexity review
Disable Semantica writes on shared folders during review
Add file-level ownership markers
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantica emphasizes deterministic provenance and decision records, while Perplexity produces cited answers from live search. If Semantica ingests Perplexity output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into knowledge graphs and downstream decisions. The pair has a clear handoff path, but Semantica's provenance features reduce, rather than eliminate, the risk.
conditions: IF Perplexity answers are ingested into Semantica without provenance checks
IF Semantica downstream consumers treat imported answers as ground truth
mitigations: Require source links for every imported claim
Compare Perplexity output against a second source
Mark imported records as unverified until reviewed
Limit automatic propagation to decision records
requires-engineering: add verification gates before graph writes

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while Semantica is self-hosted but handles enterprise data, contracts, and secrets. If EU PII or regulated enterprise data is moved from Semantica into Perplexity, residency and retention obligations can be violated because the pair lacks any documented DPA, residency control, or retention alignment in the profiles. The other agent is cited because the risk is cross-system transfer.
conditions: IF regulated or EU personal data is transferred from Semantica into Perplexity
IF no contractual or technical residency controls are configured for that transfer
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Use synthetic or anonymized records for cross-agent workflows
Document a data-transfer policy before deployment
Review retention settings on both systems
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
